inventory.test: supabase/migrations/119_job_outbox_rls.sql - guarded ALTER, BEGIN/COMMIT, SET LOCAL (production surface, Direction B)
inventory.reason: Not mutated as a unit test - measured directly against a throwaway clone, which is the stronger oracle. Guard RUNS when relrowsecurity is false (pre-119 clone -> t, client grants gone) and SKIPS when true (re-apply idempotent, predicate f). Under a concurrent ACCESS SHARE holder the guarded file completes in 64 ms while the same ALTER issued unconditionally blocks and dies at lock_timeout after 5090 ms - both halves of the header's locking claim proven, and SET LOCAL demonstrably bounds the ALTER. No NULL hazard exists: a missing relation makes the regclass cast ERROR, it never yields NULL.

findings.title: The new ACL guard filters on grantee NAME, so a grant via PUBLIC or via a role anon inherits leaves the whole suite green while anon holds INSERT on the dispatch spine
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Confirmed by mutation on a throwaway clone at HEAD, not argued. GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON job_outbox TO PUBLIC writes relacl {test=arwdDxt/test,=r/test} - grantee OID 0, whose regrole cast renders as a bare dash, so it matches neither anon nor authenticated and aclexplode returns zero rows. Whole suite: 6 passed / 0 failed. In the same state has_table_privilege('anon','public.job_outbox','SELECT') = t and has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.job_outbox','INSERT') = t. The second path is role membership: CREATE ROLE rt_mid; GRANT rt_mid TO anon; GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON job_outbox TO rt_mid leaves the oracle empty with the same effective privilege. NOT equivalent: the mutant reproduces exactly the exposure the migration header names as the reason this migration exists - anon holds INSERT, and OutboxPoller dispatches whatever rows it finds without asking who wrote them. NOT an unexecuted branch: the identical assertion FAILED under the R1 mutant. This is the P0 fix trading one blindness for another - has_table_privilege was blind to superusers but saw EFFECTIVE privilege including PUBLIC and inheritance; the aclexplode grantee-name filter is superuser-proof but sees only DIRECT grants. Graded P0 on two limbs. First, the protocol's own taxonomy: the survivor is confirmed, executed, and provably NOT equivalent, and the only non-blocking classifications require either a proof of behaviour preservation (false here) or a judgement of plausible equivalence (also false). Second, a false doc claim: the case's own header at lines 30-33 states that a future migration's GRANT is applied by pnpm test:db:setup on every container, so this case genuinely fails on that regression - measured FALSE for a GRANT TO PUBLIC. The real-world exposure is nonetheless BOUNDED, and the arbiter should size it accordingly: (a) the realistic regression, a named grant to anon or authenticated, is measurably caught, (b) neither project carries a PUBLIC table ACL entry today (introspected read-only 2026-09-07: relacl on both is {postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role}, no PUBLIC entry), (c) no migration in this repo emits a PUBLIC table grant or a role-membership grant, and (d) the branch's own sibling suite 117 keeps the complementary has_table_privilege form, so the house already owns the other half. It is a coverage gap in the branch's SOLE designated regression guard for this boundary (ci:rls-audit covers only TENANT_TABLES), not a defect in the migration. Behavioural replacement, two clauses: widen the grantee predicate to also admit acl.grantee = 0 and pg_has_role('anon', acl.grantee, 'USAGE') / pg_has_role('authenticated', acl.grantee, 'USAGE'), or keep the ACL read and add a has_table_privilege arm for the two client roles alongside it - the two oracles are blind in opposite directions and the pair is what makes the case complete.
findings.reason: FIXED by the root and verified by re-running round 2's own mutation. Title 4 now carries TWO arms. Arm A (relacl + attacl via aclexplode) admits acl.grantee = 0, so PUBLIC is no longer invisible to the NAME filter. Arm B is new and asks the effective question - has_table_privilege for anon and authenticated over a privilege list DERIVED from acldefault('r', owner) rather than spelled - which also catches a grant reaching anon through role membership, and RT-9's concatenated grant. The derivation is load-bearing: the local container is PostgreSQL 16 (7 privilege types) and both Supabase projects are 17 (8, MAINTAIN added), so a hardcoded list would miss one there or raise unrecognized privilege type here. has_table_privilege is sound for these two roles even though it was the wrong tool for the OWNER in RT-1: the superuser short-circuit does not apply to anon or authenticated, which are NOLOGIN non-superuser roles. Measured: GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON job_outbox TO PUBLIC -> suite 1 failed / 5 passed (it was 6/6 before the fix); REVOKE ALL ON job_outbox FROM PUBLIC -> 6/6. NOTE: no independent adversarial pass has run against the fixed tree - round-start refuses a third round - so this disposition rests on the root's own mutation evidence, which is disclosed to the owner rather than presented as an independent verification.

findings.title: The file-text guard forbids GRANT but not a subsequent DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so a self-cancelling migration passes every case
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Journaled mutation M9 appends ALTER TABLE job_outbox DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; inside the transaction, immediately before COMMIT. The suite reports 6 passed / 0 failed. The case at line 163 asserts the ENABLE statement is PRESENT and forbids CREATE POLICY and FORCE, but nothing forbids a later DISABLE; the statement parser never sees it either, because it starts with ALTER rather than REVOKE or GRANT. NOT equivalent: applied, the file leaves relrowsecurity false, which is precisely the staging state the branch exists to remove. NOT an unexecuted branch: all three file-text assertions run on every invocation. P2 rather than P1 because the catalogue case DOES kill it once the container is re-provisioned - measured as R3, where a behind-head clone made that case fail first with the actionable BEHIND_HEAD message - and CI provisions the database fresh on every run, so the escape exists only in the DB-free lane and only until the next pnpm test:db:setup. This is the same class round 1 filed as RT-5 (P2); the fix closed the GRANT half of it and left the DISABLE half. Behavioural replacement: add a not.toMatch assertion for DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY beside the two absence assertions already there.
findings.reason: FIXED by the root. expect(text).not.toMatch(/DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY/i) added beside the existing CREATE POLICY and FORCE assertions in the same case. A self-cancelling DISABLE below the ENABLE would leave the file reading as if it hardens the table while shipping the drift it exists to close.

findings.title: A GRANT assembled by string concatenation inside the DO block evades both text checks and really grants anon ALL
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Journaled mutation M2 appends a DO block whose EXECUTE concatenates the keyword from two string fragments. Verified valid SQL with a real effect BEFORE the test run - applied to the clone it writes relacl {test=arwdDxt/test,anon=arwdDxt/test}. Suite: 6 passed / 0 failed. It defeats the statement list because the dollar-quoted body is masked, and it defeats the raw-text counter because the keyword is never spelled. NOT equivalent, NOT unexecuted, by the same reasoning as RT-8. P2 and recorded rather than charged: this is an adversarial-author construct, not an authoring accident, and a migration-text guard's threat model is a future developer widening the file, not an attacker obfuscating inside it. The catalogue case kills it on the next provision. No behavioural replacement is proposed - a text guard cannot close this class, and the honest fix is to scope the header sentence at line 35 to what a developer would plausibly write.
findings.reason: FIXED, though not by a text guard - no text guard can see a concatenated identifier, and D17's belt cannot either. Closed by RT-7's Arm B: the concatenated GRANT genuinely executes, so the effective-privilege read observes it once pnpm test:db:setup applies the migration. This is the argument for holding a catalogue arm at all - text guards bound what the file may SAY, only the catalogue bounds what it DOES.
